predecessors.name: French Consulate
predecessors.text: France with Belgium (1795), the German left bank of the Rhine (1797), Geneva and Mulhouse (1798) and Piedmont (1802): the territory of the Consulate when 'On 18 May 1804, Napoleon was granted the…

successors.name: Kingdom of France (Bourbon Restoration and July Monarchy)
successors.text: France in its borders of 1 June 1792 with the additions of the Treaty of Paris of 30 May 1814 (Saarbrücken, Saarlouis, Landau, Montbéliard, part of Savoy, Avignon, the Comtat Venaissin)

successors.name: Sovereign Principality of the United Netherlands
successors.text: 'The Netherlands, now freed from the French empire, asked William I' to become their prince; he accepted in late 1813

successors.name: Swiss Confederation
successors.text: the Valais, annexed 1810; 'This treaty formally recognized the independence of Switzerland (Art.

successors.name: Austrian Empire
successors.text: the Illyrian Provinces, comprising the Dalmatian coast; French rule ended on 27 January 1814 (Illyrian Provinces page)

successors.name: Kingdom of Sardinia
successors.text: Piedmont, Aosta, Savoy and Nice, returned to the crown in 1814

successors.name: Grand Duchy of Tuscany
successors.text: Tuscany, re-established under Ferdinand III in 1814

successors.name: Duchy of Parma and Piacenza
successors.text: Parma, Piacenza and Guastalla given to Marie-Louise by the Treaty of Fontainebleau (11 April 1814)

successors.name: Principality of Monaco
successors.text: Monaco, Menton and Roquebrune, restored in 1814

successors.name: Kingdom of Spain
successors.text: Catalonia, annexed 1812 to the Treaty of Valençay (December 1813)

successors.name: Principality of Andorra
successors.text: Andorra, independence restored by imperial decree in 1814

successors.name: Free City of Hamburg
successors.text: Hamburg, freed after the abdication in April 1814

successors.name: Luxembourg
successors.text: Luxembourg, cleared of the French in 1814; the Grand Duchy follows in 1815

successors.name: Kingdom of Prussia
successors.text: the left bank of the Rhine north of the Palatinate, awarded to Prussia (Territorial evolution page)

ledger.x: 18 May 1804: Napoleon is granted the title of Emperor of the French.
1805: the Ligurian Republic is annexed.
25 September 1805: the Ulm campaign.
26 December 1805: the Treaty of Pressburg.
1806: France occupies Hesse-Kassel.
1806: Saxony is occupied.
1806: French troops overrun Mecklenburg-Schwerin.
26-27 May 1806: French troops occupy the republic.
12 July 1806: the Confederation of the Rhine under Napoleon as Protector.
November 1806: the French occupy the principality.
November 1806: French troops occupy Lübeck.
11 December 1806: the Treaty of Poznań.
1807: the Treaties of Tilsit (7 July 1807) create the Duchy of Warsaw 'from the Polish lands in Prussian possession' as a French client.
July 1807: the occupation becomes annexation to Westphalia.
July 1807: the Peace of Tilsit ends the occupation ('until the Peace of Tilsit in July 1807').
July 1807: Prussia cedes Bayreuth.
24 August 1807: Stralsund falls.
1 September 1807: Berthier declares the annexation of the Septinsular Republic.
15 November 1807: Westphalia joins the Confederation of the Rhine, created under the Treaties of Tilsit (7 July 1807) for Jérôme Bonaparte.
1808: Etruria and Parma are annexed.
1808: the Duchy of Parma is annexed; the counterpart slug is the Cliopatria row that restores Parma in 1815.
1808: Mecklenburg-Schwerin joins the Confederation of the Rhine ('in 1808 Frederick Francis I joined the Confederation of the Rhine').
31 January 1808: the occupation ends in annexation.
15 June 1808: Joseph Bonaparte is made King of Spain.
1809: the Papal States are annexed.
14 October 1809: the Illyrian Provinces pass to France.
4 October 1809: Britain takes Zakynthos and Cephalonia.
1810: Holland and the Valais are annexed.
1810: the Valais is annexed.
1810: France annexes Meppen and Dülmen.
1810: the Weser department leaves Westphalia.
1810: Swedish Pomerania returns to Sweden.
1810: military governments dependent on Paris.
1810: Catalonia too is a military government dependent on Paris; it is annexed in 1812.
16 April 1810: the garrison of Lefkada surrenders.
10 June 1810: Istria and Dalmatia pass from the Kingdom of Italy to the Empire.
August 1810: the French invade central Portugal.
13 December 1810: Oldenburg is annexed.
13 December 1810: Salm is annexed.
December 1810: Nord and Niederelbe pass from Westphalia to the Empire.
1811: the occupation turns into annexation.
1811: Bremen is annexed.
1811: Hamburg is annexed (same Territorial evolution entry).
1811: Lübeck is annexed.
April 1811: Massena returns to Spain.
1812: Catalonia is annexed.
1812: Andorra is annexed with Catalonia.
1812: the military government of Catalonia becomes annexation (next events).
24 June 1812: the invasion of Russia begins ('Invasion of Russia: began 24 June 1812').
14 December 1812: the Grande Armée leaves Russian territory.
Late 1813: the Netherlands are freed.
ledger.cpn: Sovereign Principality of the United Netherlands

ledger.x: 1813: Oldenburg is restored.
1813: the French leave Bremen.
1813: Lübeck is free again.
January 1813: Russia occupies most of the Duchy of Warsaw.
June 1813: Joseph permanently leaves Spain.
June 1813: Joseph 'permanently left Spain in June'.
26 October 1813: Prussian troops occupy Westphalia.
October 1813: the Hanoverian north is freed.
4 November 1813: the Confederation of the Rhine is dissolved.
December 1813: the Treaty of Valençay.
1814: Andorra's independence is restored.
1814: Hamburg is freed.
27 January 1814: the last French garrison in the Illyrian Provinces surrenders.
30 May 1814: Switzerland's independence is recognised ('This treaty formally recognized the independence of Switzerland (Art.
Spring 1814: the Low Countries are cleared of the French.
ledger.cpn: Sovereign Principality of the United Netherlands

ledger.x: 1814: Luxembourg leaves French hands with the Low Countries.
1814: Piedmont returns to the crown.
1814: Savoy (except Annecy and Chambéry) and Nice return to the crown.
1814: Liguria leaves the Empire; the republic is restored on 28 April 1814, briefly, before the Congress gives Liguria to Sardinia.
1814: Tuscany is lost.
1814: the Papal States are restored.
11 April 1814: the duchies are given to Marie-Louise.
1814: the Grimaldi return.
1814: the left bank of the Rhine leaves French hands.
1814: the Palatinate passes to the Allies.
April-June 1814: Corfu is evacuated.
ledger.cpn: United States of the Ionian Islands

ledger.x: 6 April 1814: the First French Empire ends.
ledger.cpn: Kingdom of France (Bourbon Restoration and July Monarchy)

wars.name: War of the Third Coalition
wars.outcome: French victory at Ulm (October 1805) and Austerlitz (early December 1805); 'On 26 December 1805, Austria and France signed the Treaty of Pressburg': Austria ceded land to Bavaria, Württemberg and Baden and Venetia went to the Kingdom of Italy.

wars.name: War of the Fourth Coalition
wars.outcome: Jena-Auerstedt (1806), Friedland (1807), the Treaties of Tilsit of 7 July 1807: the Kingdom of Westphalia and the Duchy of Warsaw are created.

wars.name: War of the Fifth Coalition
wars.outcome: The Treaty of Schönbrunn, 14 October 1809, gives France the Illyrian Provinces.

wars.name: Peninsular War
wars.outcome: France annexes only Catalonia and Andorra (1812); the rest of Cliopatria's Spanish cells are client and occupied ground.

wars.name: French invasion of Russia
wars.outcome: The invasion 'began 24 June 1812'; Napoleon entered Moscow (undated) and the army was driven back.

wars.name: War of the Sixth Coalition
wars.outcome: Coalition victory: Leipzig (16-19 October 1813), the Frankfurt proposals (November 1813, withdrawn by December), the invasion of France in 1814, the Allies in Paris on 31 March 1814, Napoleon's abdication (11 April 1814 on this page) and the Treaty of Paris…

certainty.note: The annexed departments are administrative lines dated by decree; the client states (Warsaw, Westphalia, the Confederation) have approximate outlines in Cliopatria and are not the empire's land.
The 1812 invasion ground and the shrinking frontier of 1813-1814 are approximate; the borders of 1 June 1792 confirmed by the Treaty of Paris of 30 May 1814 are sharp from the treaty.
